claim: Hundreds of S-21’s own staff were executed, according to its records.
fix: Removed. Replaced with what the US Holocaust Memorial Museum documents: S-21 mostly held the regime’s own cadres.

claim: Only a handful of the at least 14,000 prisoners survived.
fix: Made precise: 14,000–17,000 held, about 12 believed to have survived.

claim: Does the government admit it? “Denied.”
fix: Re-rated “yes”: Cambodia’s governments since 1979 recognise the crimes and helped set up the tribunal; the Khmer Rouge leaders were the ones who denied.

claim: About 25,000 to 35,000 detained; deaths and suicides in the hundreds.
fix: Replaced with the documented counts (at least 72 deaths, 180 suicides) and the full range of estimates (25,000–38,000).

claim: Floods in July and August 1995 hit perhaps 30% of the country.
fix: Kept. UN assessment and encyclopedia sources added.

claim: North Korea has not released a full death count.
fix: Fixed: its officials have given about 220,000–235,000, far below outside estimates.

claim: 14–20 million Chinese died in the war with Japan.
fix: Kept. Source added.

claim: Mao himself later said about 700,000 had been killed (1950–53).
fix: Reworded: the figure comes from the unpublished version of a 1957 speech and cannot be checked against the published text.

claim: About 17 million urban youths were sent to the countryside.
fix: Kept. Scholars give 17 to 20 million.

claim: Memorial compiled about 3 million names before Russian courts closed it in 2021.
fix: Updated: the database stayed online until April 2026, when Russia’s Supreme Court labelled Memorial “extremist”.

claim: The UAE paid a Geneva firm to run smear campaigns in Europe (Abu Dhabi Secrets).
fix: Kept, with the documented scale (at least €5.7 million; over 1,000 people in 18 countries) and three sources from different regions.

claim: Intent rated “disputed”, while China’s famine with the same kind of evidence was rated “knew and kept going”.
fix: Re-rated “knew and kept going”, with the separate genocide debate still shown as disputed.

claim: US intent rated more gently than communist cases with the same evidence.
fix: Re-rated “knew and kept going”.

claim: A quote credited to Stalin.
fix: Credited to Molotov, who said it.

claim: “563 S-21 staff were executed.”
fix: Removed; the number could not be sourced.

claim: A reported execution of North Korea’s army chief, Ri Yong-gil (2016).
fix: Now says the report proved false when he reappeared alive.

claim: Length of China’s high-speed rail.
fix: Updated to about 50,400 km, over 70% of the world total (UIC).

claim: The high death toll stated as settled.
fix: Added Gareth Porter’s finding that the high US figures rested on misused documents.

claim: The crackdown described without the events the government cites.
fix: Added the 2009 Ürümqi riots and the 2013–14 militant attacks.

claim: An older count of detention sites.
fix: Updated to over 380 sites found by ASPI satellite research.

claim: A vague figure for peasants stopped at the borders.
fix: Made precise: about 220,000 caught in one month, from the security police’s own report.

claim: An AI treaty mentioned without its source.
fix: Named: the Council of Europe’s 2024 framework convention.
